title: "Getting Started"

See [Overview](index.qmd#installation) for installation instructions.

## Authentication

Credentials depend on which `STACSource` you use, and only one is needed:

- **`MPCSource`** needs no credentials -- Planetary Computer data is
  anonymously accessible. Anonymous access carries lower rate limits and
  shorter-lived access tokens, though, which can cause failures on large
  concurrent runs, and Microsoft's subscription keys, which formerly
  raised those limits, are no longer obtainable since the developer
  portal that issued them was retired.
- **`OPERASource`** (NASA OPERA RTC-S1 via ASF/CMR) requires a NASA
  Earthdata Login. Create a free account at
  [urs.earthdata.nasa.gov](https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov), then set up
  a `~/.netrc` entry for it. The recommended way is the built-in helper:
  ```python
  from autofloods.authenticate import setup_earthdata_login

  setup_earthdata_login()
  ```
  For scripted or non-interactive setup, pass credentials directly
  instead of prompting (e.g. from an environment variable or secrets
  manager):
  ```python
  setup_earthdata_login(username=my_username, password=my_password)
  ```
  You can also set up `~/.netrc` by hand:
  ```
  machine urs.earthdata.nasa.gov
    login your-username
    password your-password
  ```
  ```bash
  chmod 600 ~/.netrc
  ```

  `OPERASource` also requires the GDAL command-line tools
  (`gdalbuildvrt`) to be installed separately -- see
  [Installation](index.qmd#installation) for the `apt-get`/`conda`
  commands.

## Running AutoFloods

There are two ways to run AutoFloods: the `flood_mapper` class directly
in a notebook/script (more control), or a config file + the runner
script (fastest way to launch a real job, no code to write). Both use
the same underlying pipeline and produce the same output. See
[Examples](examples.qmd) for grid generation and full walkthroughs of
both.
